clue.text: Artist brought back to design flat

indicators.note: brought back says the letters for artist are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter returns to a drawing board to create something flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Planar is the geometric adjective for lying in a single plane, i.e. level and even.

clue.text: Landowner's no duke — a flashy Australian

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter for duke is dropped from the word

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: An estate holder turns out to be no aristocrat, just a showy Aussie.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAIRD is a Scottish landed proprietor; in Australian slang a lair is a flashily dressed show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang term for a vulgar show-off who dresses loudly.

clue.text: Organised pen operator lacks nothing, right? May have this, then

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lacks says the letters for nothing and right are removed from the words before them

explanation.surface: A tidy typist missing nothing is asked whether they keep the stationery to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes O (nothing) and R (right) from PEN OPERATOR, leaving PENPEATOR for 'Organised' to rearrange. The definition leans on the whole clue: a pen operator, a writer, may well have this.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper is exactly what a person wielding a pen would be expected to possess.

clue.text: Scout's idea that might be taken on?

definitions.meaning: a scout or messenger sent ahead, one who carries word on foot

definitions.text: idea that might be taken on
definitions.meaning: a viable proposal, as opposed to a non-starter that nobody would adopt

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a messenger and a feasible proposal are called by this word; the second is the opposite of a non-runner.

clue.text: Location without work diminished the community

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the location wraps round the work
diminished means made smaller, so the work loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A site with no employment has worn down its local people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking: the trimmed work sits inside the location.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace means the ordinary people of a place, the general community.

clue.text: Distraught dope-needer, I push drug

indicators.note: distraught means badly agitated, so these letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: An addict in withdrawal confesses to dealing narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A decongestant medicine, it is a drug in the pharmaceutical sense.

clue.text: Hope for only half the people at the match?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: only half says just the first five of the ten letters are used

parts.note: the crowd at a match are its spectators

explanation.surface: A wish that only half the crowd at a game might share.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten-letter crowd word is cut to its first five letters by 'only half'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is an expectation or hope of something to come.

clue.text: What could give a hit to criminal's bottom?

definitions.text: What could give a hit to criminal's bottom?

indicators.note: bottom in a down clue means the last letter of the word
could give suggests the letters are made to yield a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A riddle about what might deliver a blow to a villain's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' gives L, the last letter of criminal's, and 'could give' rearranges A HIT into ATHI. A lathi is the heavy bamboo stick carried by Indian police.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian policeman's iron-bound stick, well suited to whacking an offender's rear.

clue.text: Like some rings using trick to get money — prosperous, no end

parts.note: a cent is a small unit of money

indicators.note: no end says the last letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A swindler cashes in on rings through endless trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' trims RICH to RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentric circles share a common centre, as tree rings or ripples do.

clue.text: Attitude taken by girl showing aloofness

indicators.note: taken by places the attitude after the girl, as if she carries it along

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A young woman's pose reveals her coolness.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping one's distance means holding oneself apart; reserve or coolness of manner.

clue.text: Sally's exposure

definitions.meaning: a sally is a jaunt or excursion
public revealing of someone, especially of their sexuality

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip out and the public revealing of a person's secret share this one word.

clue.text: 22-9 4? I sped, I hied, fantastically full of double power

indicators.note: full of says the shuffled letters enclose the doubled power
fantastically means wildly, so these letters are rearranged
double says the letter for power appears twice

explanation.surface: A runner boasts of racing and hurrying with incredible strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastically' rearranges I SPED I HIED around PP, the 'double' of power. The cross-reference reads as 'long distance runner' (22, 9 and 4 together).
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek messenger ran from Athens to Sparta before Marathon, the archetypal long-distance runner.

clue.text: Appropriate name given to animal with butterfly on

parts.note: the comma is a species of butterfly

explanation.surface: A suitable label is given to a creature with a butterfly perched on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts COMMA above N + DEER ('given to' attaching the name).
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take for one's own use, as officials seize property.

clue.text: Group of office workers about to supply part of computer program

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a typing pool is a group of office workers

explanation.surface: Clerical staff are on hand to provide a piece of software.
explanation.definitionFit: In programming, a section of instructions repeated until a condition is met.

clue.text: Mount with a castle destroyed by foe ultimately

indicators.note: destroyed means knocked down and broken up, so these letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A climb on a fortress that an enemy finally demolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' turns A CASTLE into ESCALAT, and 'ultimately' adds E from foe.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to climb or increase, like mounting tension.

clue.text: Gangster, turning up and working for journalist, moved illegally

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue says the letters read upwards

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster
under means working for, subordinate to
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A mobster takes a job with a reporter and smuggles goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' turns AL into LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundered money is moved through legitimate channels to hide its criminal source.

clue.text: Rabbit? Not a 22-9 4

parts.note: Updike's hero nicknamed Rabbit bears this surname; the same word is a tiny unit of length, hardly a long distance, and he runs in Rabbit, Run

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference reads 'long distance runner'. The surname of Updike's Rabbit is also a minute unit of length, ten to the minus ten metres.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Updike's Rabbit is also a unit of length so tiny it is the opposite of a long distance.

clue.text: Tirade with nursemaid about to become purple

indicators.note: about says the nursemaid goes round the tirade

parts.note: an amah is a nursemaid in East Asia

explanation.surface: An angry outburst from a nanny makes her go red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: AMAH is an East or South Asian nursemaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaranth is a purplish-red colour named after the flower.

clue.text: The one often seen with 16

definitions.meaning: a single item, as in one counted thing
the tiny length is often followed by this word, as in angstrom ___

explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, and the angstrom is a unit of length often named with it.

clue.text: Cave in which British and German kings meet

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the cipher of British kings
Otto was the name of several German kings and emperors

explanation.surface: Monarchs from Britain and Germany hold a meeting underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kings' serves both: GR (George Rex) for the British, OTTO for the German.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave.

clue.text: Mac's remarkable northern team — looking hot but ignored

parts.note: unco is Scots for remarkable; Mac is a Scot

explanation.surface: A Scot's fine northern football team looks good but goes unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mac stands for a Scot in crosswords, signalling a Scots word: UNCO, meaning remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unconsidered has been disregarded, passed over without thought.

clue.text: Officer conveying Her Majesty, one behaving as conductor would?

indicators.note: conveying means carrying, so the officer holds the other letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A commander escorts the Queen, a figure acting like an orchestra leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'conductor' is electrical, not musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An ohmic conductor obeys Ohm's law, its current proportional to voltage.

clue.text: Bit of wood covering one end of kitchen is pine

indicators.note: covering says the wood surrounds the chosen letter

parts.note: a log is a bit of wood

indicators.note: one end of picks out a single terminal letter, here the last

explanation.surface: A piece of timber in the kitchen turns out to be pine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one end of' takes N from kitchen, which goes inside LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to long, to yearn for something absent.

clue.text: Ball in sewer

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a delivery that deviates off the stitching of the ball
one who sews, a stitcher of seams

explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain but means one who sews. In cricket a bowler gets the ball to move off its raised stitching, its seam.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket delivery that moves off the seam, and a person who sews seams, share this word.

clue.text: To get rid of trouble-maker finally introduce supranational crime busters

indicators.note: to get rid of says the trouble-maker's letters are removed from the word
finally places the removal at the end of the word

parts.note: to interpolate is to introduce or insert
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: To be rid of a troublesome person, bring in the international police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To get rid of' with 'finally' cuts ATE from the end of INTERPOLATE. Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol coordinates police cooperation across nations, an international crime-fighting body.

clue.text: Chair made to shake — I extracted old coins

indicators.note: to shake means to jiggle about, so these letters are rearranged
extracted says the letter I is pulled out of the word chair

explanation.surface: A rickety seat, made to wobble, has had its occupant pulled out, revealing ancient money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted' removes I from CHAIR, leaving CHAR, which 'to shake' rearranges with MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Drachmae is the plural of drachma, the currency of ancient and pre-euro Greece.

clue.text: What can one do in this phase? My goodness, look back!

definitions.text: What can one do in this phase?

indicators.note: back says the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: egad is an exclamation like my goodness
lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: An elderly person exclaims at the thought of looking over their past.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'look back', turns EGADLO into OLDAGE. The definition hints that in later life one can only exclaim and look back.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stage of life, a time often spent reminiscing over the years gone by.
